system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Basis:** Buyer Negotiation Playbook; Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter dated 22 September 2026 (untrusted counterparty material).

## Overall assessment

The Seller's cover note describes the package as "fair and balanced." It is not. Almost every limitation and risk-allocation point has been set at or beyond the Seller-favourable end, and several provisions interact to collapse our separate protections into a single, capped, time-limited, knowledge-barred general regime. The Disclosure Letter, by contrast, is candid in places and actually confirms several of our concerns (no Bluefen consent, no Riverlark payout, bonuses not in funds flow). We should use those admissions.

Note on authority: the 20% / AUD 4.8m cap and the 18-month claims period happen to match our fallback numbers. That does **not** make them cleared. Playbook sec 0.4/6.3: a position is not accepted because a number matches a fallback; both require prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft, and none has been given. We respond at our starting positions.

---

## 1. Liability architecture

### 1.1 General warranty cap – Clause 12.1
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
- **Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000 opening; 20% only with Amelia Frost written authority (none given).
- **Position:** Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not signal that 20% is within range. If the deal team wants to table 20% later, that is a separate authority request to Amelia Frost referencing this draft.

### 1.2 Thresholds – Clause 12.2
- **Seller:** de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; **excess-only** recovery.
- **Playbook:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; **first-dollar** (tipping) recovery.
- **Reasoning:** The Seller's numbers are 5x ours on both thresholds, and the switch from tipping to deductible is a structural change that writes off the first AUD 250,000 of every valid aggregate claim. On a AUD 24m deal, individual claims under AUD 25,000 could cover a substantial proportion of typical post-completion issues (e.g. employee on-costs, supplier invoices, minor tax adjustments).
- **Position:** Reject all three elements; counter at AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 / first-dollar.

### 1.3 Time limits – Clause 12.3 / 13
- **Seller:** 18 months for general claims; **plus** "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Playbook:** 24 months; 18 months only with Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- **Reasoning:** Two issues. The 18-month period is a fallback we are not authorised to accept. More seriously, the second sentence is a default-rule that makes every limitation universal unless we carve out each exception affirmatively. Combined with 1.4–1.5 below, it is the mechanism by which Title, Tax, IP, indemnities and fraud would fall under the general cap and clock.
- **Position:** 24 months. Delete the "applies to all Claims" default; replace with the opposite default – limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims and only where expressly stated.

### 1.4 Fundamental / Title warranties
- **Seller:** same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."
- **Playbook:** separate regime – 100% cap, minimum six years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- **Reasoning:** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason. If the Seller does not own the shares or lacks capacity, we have paid AUD 24m for nothing; a AUD 4.8m cap and 18-month window is unacceptable. This is non-negotiable in substance.
- **Position:** Reject. Require a separate Fundamental Warranty schedule with its own regime per the playbook.

### 1.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance – Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5
- **Seller:** apply "to all Claims of any nature."
- **Playbook:** fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance; categories kept separate.
- **Reasoning:** As drafted, there is no fraud carve-out at all. Beyond being contrary to the playbook, an attempt to limit liability for fraud is of doubtful enforceability and would attract scrutiny from any sensible reviewer. "All Claims of any nature" also sweeps in the specific indemnities (Ironquay), Tax, IP and title claims. Note the Seller separately describes Tax/IP as "settled under the general regime above" – that is the same override by a different route.
- **Position:** Insert an express fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out from every limitation, the exclusive-remedy clause and the non-reliance clause, to the maximum extent enforceable. Confirm expressly that Title, Tax, IP, payment covenants and specific indemnities are outside clauses 12.1–12.3 and 20.5 unless stated otherwise. No one on our side may waive the fraud carve-out.

---

## 2. Disclosure and knowledge

### 2.1 General disclosure – Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.2]
- **Seller:** everything in the data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and publicly searchable records deemed disclosed.
- **Playbook:** specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Reasoning:** Data-room-wide disclosure converts every document into a qualification of every warranty, regardless of whether a reasonable buyer would identify the issue. "Publicly searchable records" is open-ended. Paragraph [1.4] (nothing admits breach, liability or materiality) is a standard reservation but, combined with general disclosure, means the Seller discloses everything and admits nothing.
- **Position:** Delete [1.1] and [1.2] as general disclosures. Replace with a fair-disclosure standard: a matter is disclosed only if it is disclosed in the Disclosure Letter with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter. Specific paragraphs 2–10 can stand as specific disclosures, subject to our review of each.

### 2.2 Buyer knowledge – Clause 8.3
- **Seller:** no claim for any matter of which the Buyer "or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records."
- **Playbook:** delete blanket knowledge exclusions; any qualifier limited to named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Reasoning:** This is the broadest form of the exclusion: it extends to advisers, to constructive knowledge ("discoverable"), and to public records. Read with 2.1 it effectively bars any claim on any matter touched by the data room, converting the warranties into a nullity. It also sits with the "all Claims" override so that title and fraud would be barred by knowledge.
- **Position:** Delete clause 8.3 entirely. Seller knowledge qualifiers in warranties (if any) to be by reference to a short list of named Seller individuals after due and careful enquiry. Express statement that no Buyer knowledge (actual, constructive or imputed) limits Title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnity claims.

---

## 3. Completion-critical matters

### 3.1 Bluefen consent – Clause 3 / 6.3
- **Seller:** "addressed"; reasonable endeavours; consent satisfied "on delivery of the counterparty's written consent."
- **Disclosure Letter para 2:** ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30% of revenue); clause 11.2 change-control consent with conditions in 11.3; **no final written consent and no evidence conditions are satisfied** as at 22 September.
- **Playbook:** effective consent AND evidence conditions satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours insufficient for a material customer.
- **Reasoning:** The Seller's own disclosure contradicts the cover note's "addressed." Bluefen is ~30% of revenue; a conditional consent whose conditions are unmet is not a consent. "Delivery of written consent" could be satisfied by a letter with unsatisfied conditions precedent. Reasonable endeavours is the lowest endeavours standard.
- **Position:** Condition precedent must be (a) effective, unconditional (or with all conditions satisfied and evidenced) consent under clause 11.2/11.3 in a form approved by the Buyer, (b) delivered before Completion. Seller obligation to be "all reasonable endeavours" or "best endeavours" with Buyer information rights on the consent process. Buyer-only waiver right. We should also obtain a copy of the Bluefen contract (DD-002) and form our own view on clause 11.3 conditions.

### 3.2 Riverlark facility – Clause 2 / 7
- **Seller:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion."
- **Disclosure Letter para 3:** not repaid; no final discharge of security in the data room; change-of-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2.
- **Playbook:** current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases at Completion; post-completion release requires irrevocable undertaking plus Amelia Frost approval.
- **Reasoning:** This is a debt-free/cash-free deal. A post-completion release leaves us owning a company whose assets remain secured to Riverlark, with a change-of-control trigger (8.1) that may already have been breached on Completion. We would be dependent on the Seller and the bank performing after we have paid. The Seller's "approximately" AUD 3.2m is not a payout figure.
- **Position:** Require (a) a Riverlark payout letter dated no earlier than a few business days before Completion, (b) repayment direct from Completion funds via the funds flow with a corresponding price adjustment, (c) executed security releases/PPSR discharges and Riverlark's consent/waiver of 8.1 delivered at Completion. If the Seller insists on post-completion mechanics, that is an escalation to Amelia Frost, not a point we accept, and would need an irrevocable bank undertaking in any event.

### 3.3 Employee bonuses – DD-005 / funds flow
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 bonuses "a matter for the Seller," not itemised in the funds flow.
- **Disclosure Letter para 5:** bonuses triggered on Completion and continued employment; **not in draft funds flow**; silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- **Playbook:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Reasoning:** "A matter for the Seller" is a statement of intent, not a mechanism. The bonuses are Company obligations triggered by Completion; if unfunded at Completion, the Company (now ours) pays them, and we have paid the price twice. On-costs (super, payroll tax, possibly leave loading) are not quantified; a rough rule of thumb is that they could add a meaningful percentage on top, but we should have the Seller quantify rather than assume.
- **Position:** Funds flow to show a specific line for AUD 420,000 plus quantified on-costs, treated as Debt-like / deducted from the price, or paid by the Seller into the Company before Completion with evidence. Warranty that there are no other Completion-triggered payments. Require the Seller to state the on-cost figure.

---

## 4. Contingent liabilities and specific matters

### 4.1 Ironquay IP – Clause 11.1
- **Seller:** indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate."
- **Disclosure Letter para 4:** DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open, not independently verified; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in data room.
- **Playbook:** broaden the narrow indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure; AUD 180,000 not independently verified either way.
- **Reasoning:** The real exposure is not the AUD 180,000 but the IP: on the Seller's own disclosure, title to SOW3 Project Materials has not passed. An indemnity capped at the fee does not cover loss of use, re-development, infringement claims by Ironquay, or customer impact if those materials are in product. We should not accept the AUD 180,000 as established either way – it is the Seller's own ledger.
- **Position:** (a) Pre-Completion: Seller to procure payment of all outstanding SOW3 fees and a confirmatory assignment of SOW3 Project Materials from Ironquay (the cure route), with evidence. (b) Indemnity to cover all loss arising from any failure of IP to vest, any Ironquay claim, and costs of cure, not merely the fee. (c) Indemnity outside the general cap/basket/time limits. (d) Request bank evidence of payments to Ironquay to verify the DD-010 figure.

### 4.2 Export/privacy incident – Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 / DD-006
- **Seller:** "preliminary operational matter," "not expected to be material."
- **Disclosure Letter para 6:** download link sent to unintended external address; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps); unknown whether accessed; investigation preliminary; not characterised as a confirmed breach; no loss amount.
- **Playbook:** preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way.
- **Reasoning:** The Seller's characterisation ("not expected to be material") is an opinion we do not adopt, but equally we should not overstate it. The facts are open. Our concern is process: we need the investigation completed, or at least progressed with records preserved, before we inherit the Company and any notification decision. Notifiable-breach analysis under the Privacy Act depends on facts (access, likelihood of serious harm) that are not yet established.
- **Position:** (a) Pre-Completion covenant: preserve all logs and evidence; complete or materially progress the investigation; provide written updates; no destruction of records. (b) Buyer to be consulted on any regulator/individual notification decision before Completion. (c) Specific indemnity for loss arising from the DD-006 incident (regulatory, notification, third-party claims, remediation), outside general limitations. (d) No price adjustment proposed at this stage – no quantified exposure.

### 4.3 Sandbar renewals – DD-008 / DD-011
- **Seller:** ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Disclosure Letter para 8:** three renewals of AUD 110,000 each; silent on whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Playbook:** assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Reasoning:** The Seller asserts ordinary course; its own Disclosure Letter declines to confirm it. We need the terms (timing, termination rights, whether accrued pre-Completion) before classifying. If renewals were triggered or committed pre-Completion for post-Completion benefit, there may be a working capital or Debt-like argument; if genuinely recurring operating costs, probably not.
- **Position:** Request DD-008/DD-011 contract terms and renewal dates; ask the Seller to confirm in the Disclosure Letter whether each is terminable and when accrued. Reserve position on treatment pending that; no deduction proposed yet.

### 4.4 Tax / IP warranties
- **Seller:** "settled under the general regime above."
- **Playbook:** OPEN; separate categories; no unlimited liability assumed, no resolution.
- **Position:** State in our mark-up that Tax and IP are not agreed and remain open; they are to be addressed as separate categories (tax indemnity, IP warranties) with their own limitation regime to be negotiated. Nothing in this draft resolves them.

### 4.5 Title evidence – DD-012
- **Seller:** title evidenced by the Company share register.
- **Disclosure Letter para 10:** register is "the source relied on" and the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- **Playbook:** independent evidence; DD-012 is a supplied internal source.
- **Reasoning:** A company-maintained share register is prima facie evidence between members but it is the Seller's own document. The Disclosure Letter fairly flags that we have not verified it.
- **Position:** Run our own ASIC company search and PPSR search against the Company and the Seller; obtain certified copies of share certificates, constitution, board minutes approving the original allotment/any transfers, and a Seller director's certificate on title, capacity and authority; require the Seller to deliver the register and ASIC Form 484 lodgement at Completion. Fundamental warranties on title/capacity under the separate regime (1.4 above).

### 4.6 Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
- Disclosure Letter says the lease carries a notification obligation (not consent) and the Mossvale assignment restriction is not triggered by a share sale.
- **Position:** Reasonable on their face, but verify both clauses ourselves. Require the landlord notification to be given pre-Completion (or as a Completion deliverable). Confirm the Mossvale clause has no change-of-control limb.

---

## 5. Structural / drafting points

- **Internal consistency:** The cover note's "addressed," "adequate," "settled," "evidenced" characterisations are not supported by the Seller's own Disclosure Letter. We should say so in our response – it strengthens our position and avoids any later argument that we accepted those characterisations.
- **"Agreed price mechanics":** The Seller says the funds flow "reflects the agreed price mechanics." We have agreed nothing in the funds flow; it omits Riverlark payout and bonuses. Treat as not agreed.
- **Reservation [11]:** The Seller's own reservation says no negotiation position or approval is included and we must evaluate against the full record. We should mirror that: our mark-up is without prejudice and subject to completion of due diligence.
- **Authority:** Any movement off 25% / AUD 6m or 24 months is an escalation to Amelia Frost, in writing, identifying the draft. Nothing here changes that.

---

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Our response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | General cap (12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | Reject; 25% / AUD 6.0m. 20% not authorised. |
| 2 | Thresholds (12.2) | AUD 25k / AUD 250k / excess-only | Reject; AUD 5k / AUD 50k / first-dollar. |
| 3 | Claims period (12.3/13) | 18 months + "all limitations apply to all Claims" | 24 months; delete universal-application default. 18 months not authorised. |
| 4 | Fundamental/Title | Same as general | Separate regime: 100% cap, 6+ years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar. |
| 5 | Limitations/non-reliance (9.3/12.8/20.5) | Apply to all Claims | Carve out fraud, wilful concealment, deliberate misconduct from everything; keep Title/Tax/IP/indemnities/covenants separate. |
| 6 | Disclosure (Sch 7, DL 1.1–1.2) | Whole data room + public records | Delete general disclosure; fair specific disclosure standard only. |
| 7 | Buyer knowledge (8.3) | Blanket incl. advisers and "discoverable" | Delete; named-person Seller knowledge qualifiers only; never applies to title, capacity, fraud, indemnities. |
| 8 | Bluefen (3/6.3) | Reasonable endeavours; consent-on-delivery | CP: effective consent with 11.3 conditions satisfied and evidenced pre-Completion; higher endeavours standard; Buyer-only waiver. |
| 9 | Riverlark (2/7) | Post-Completion release | Payout letter, repayment from Completion funds, security releases and 8.1 waiver at Completion. Post-completion only via irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval. |
| 10 | Bonuses (DD-005) | Not in funds flow | AUD 420k + quantified on-costs as a specific line item or Seller-funded with evidence. |
| 11 | Ironquay (11.1) | Indemnity limited to SOW3 fee | Pre-Completion cure (payment + confirmatory assignment); broad IP indemnity outside limitations; verify the AUD 180k. |
| 12 | DD-006 incident | "Not material" | Preserve logs, investigate, updates, consultation on notification; specific indemnity; no price adjustment yet. |
| 13 | Sandbar renewals | Ordinary course | Assess on contract terms; no classification or deduction yet. |
| 14 | Tax/IP | "Settled under general regime" | Not agreed; remain open as separate categories. |
| 15 | Title (DD-012) | Share register | Independent ASIC/PPSR searches, certificates, minutes, director's certificate. |
| 16 | Lease / Mossvale | Notification only / not triggered | Verify; landlord notification as Completion deliverable. |

**Priority order for the mark-up:** (i) fraud carve-out and separate Fundamental/Title regime, (ii) delete general disclosure and clause 8.3, (iii) Bluefen and Riverlark as Completion mechanics, (iv) caps/thresholds/time limits at playbook opening positions, (v) bonuses in funds flow, (vi) Ironquay and DD-006 specific indemnities, (vii) remaining diligence requests.

Nothing in the Seller's package should be treated as agreed, market, or final. I can prepare a clause-by-clause mark-up or the covering response letter if useful.
=== END ADVICE ===
